claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
HCL code can be converted to Pulumi.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.
In Pulumi TypeScript, `new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` and `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieve an output from another stack.
The `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (from @pulumi/terraform) accepts `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference a Terraform state stored in S3.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` exposes a `getOutput(name)` method to read outputs from the referenced Terraform state.
`aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, where `logging: "DEFAULT"` is a valid value.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The `pulumi import` CLI takes arguments in the form `<type> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
`terraform.state.S3Reference.getOutput("resources")` returns a value that can be awaited and filtered as an array of resources with `type` and `name` properties.
Pulumi provides an import API that can be used programmatically to import resources.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
`@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and policies accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` fields.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be `public-read` or `public-read-write`.
The Pulumi Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` and provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` taking `stackName`, `projectName`, and `program`.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
The Automation API stack object provides `setConfig(key, {value})` and `up({ onOutput })` methods, and `up` returns a result with `outputs`.
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
Pulumi component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team.
The `@pulumi/terraform` package exports a `terraform.state.S3Reference` type.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` constructor takes (type, name, args, opts) and `registerOutputs` is used to register outputs.
`aws.lb.LoadBalancer` accepts `name`, `loadBalancerType: "application"`, `subnets`, and `internal` arguments.

`aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` accepts `family`, `networkMode: "awsvpc"`, `requiresCompatibilities: ["FARGATE"]`, `cpu`, `memory`, and `containerDefinitions` arguments; cpu "256" with memory "512" is a valid Fargate combination.
`aws.ecs.Service` accepts `cluster`, `taskDefinition`, `desiredCount`, `launchType: "FARGATE"`, and `networkConfiguration` with `subnets` and `assignPublicIp`.
